Hi Sarah — thanks, and apologies for the slightly longer timeline; we wanted to validate a few technical details before sending. Attached are the redacted artifacts: Redwood_DPA_Annex_v2.pdf and redwood-crossborder-evidence-matrix-2025-09.xlsx. Below are concise answers to your follow-ups (inline).

1) Retention windows
- Hosted API: default telemetry & metadata retention = 90 days; request payloads (customer-configurable) = default 30 days. We can offer a 90-day option for raw inputs for debugging via contract amendment (adds minimal storage cost).
- DSAR deletion SLA: we commit to responding to verified DSARs and deleting customer-specified data within 30 calendar days. For model KV cache eviction related to a DSAR, we document the eviction request and confirm completion within the 30-day window.
- Per-customer retention scoping: yes, retention windows are configurable per account in both Hosted and Dedicated modes; for Hosted this is enforced via tenant-level configuration and lifecycle policies.

2) Encryption & keys
- Encryption at rest: AES-256 at rest for object stores and local caches; TLS 1.2+ in transit.
- BYOK for hosted: supported via integrations with major cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). Keys remain in customer-managed KMS and never exported; Redwood stores wrapped keys and performs envelope encryption. For additional key isolation (HSM-backed) we offer Dedicated/Private deployments with HSM options.

3) Subprocessors & notices
- We provide a region-level subprocessor list in the evidence matrix. We commit to a 60–90 day notification window for material subprocessor changes; the DPA annex includes an objection process (standard: review + written notice, negotiation).

4) DPF mapping (EU -> US / EU -> APAC)
- Primary legal basis: SCCs (we rely on updated EU SCCs for EU -> third-country transfers) plus contractual commitments in the DPA annex.
- Japan / Singapore: no local transfer restriction prohibits transfers to Redwood-hosted infrastructure; our matrix calls out local obligations (e.g., record-keeping for PDPA) and the technical controls (encryption, region pinning). We flag any country-specific limitations in the spreadsheet.

5) Logs schema (redacted example)
- Included in the evidence matrix: field names and types (timestamp, request_id, tenant_id, route, latency_ms, token_count, error_code). We do not include raw request inputs in the redacted pack.

Next steps: 
- If that addresses Legal's questions, I propose a 30-minute technical Q&A on Sep 23 or Sep 24. Which time works for Pioneer?
- If you want the DPA annex executed, here's the DocuSign link (redwood-dpa-pioneer-2025): https://www.docusign.com/link/redwood-pnr-dpa-2025 (placeholder).

If you need further meat on HSM architecture or exact SIEM export playbooks, Karthik will join the call.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward quickly.
